title: AI Incident Triage
summary: Stabilize an AI-enabled service, classify impact, preserve privacy-safe evidence, reconcile uncertain actions, and route decisions to accountable humans.
prerequisites: An incident response policy with severity and notification rules
On-call ownership for application, data, security, safety, and business decisions
Approved evidence retention and communication channels

sections.title: Protect people and stabilize the service
paragraphs: If credible harm is ongoing, use the fastest approved control: pause a route, disable a tool, revoke a compromised test identity, fail closed, reduce exposure, or restore a verified configuration. Preserve life-safety and emergency procedures outside the AI system. Do not wait for perfect root cause before bounded containment.

Set severity from actual and credible potential impact across people, rights, safety, privacy, security, money, availability, data integrity, compliance, and recoverability. Identify affected tenants, users, versions, models, prompts, tools, data, regions, and time windows. Track confirmed facts, hypotheses, unknowns, decisions, owners, and timestamps separately.

sections.title: Maintain a decision-ready incident record
paragraphs: Preserve correlation identifiers, configuration versions, deployment events, redacted traces, alerts, user reports, evaluation results, external-state checks, and communication decisions. Restrict raw prompts, outputs, and tool data by purpose and access; a broad incident channel is not an approved data store. Give legal, privacy, safety, security, and provider escalation owners the evidence their policies require.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes impact and severity rationale, bounded scope, verified containment, a timestamped decision log, privacy-safe traces, external-state reconciliation, owners, communications, and recovery criteria. Verify each containment control in the actual affected boundary, confirm error and harm signals stop, check data and tool postconditions, and keep monitoring through the declared observation window.

Stop expansion or automated operation when harm grows, protected data is exposed, write outcomes are unknown, observability is lost, ownership is unclear, or the current configuration cannot be proven. Recovery means maintaining containment, restoring or failing over to a verified path under human authority, reconciling every consequential operation, communicating by policy, and deferring closeout until durable fixes and recurrence checks exist.
sections.callout: Containment may precede root cause, but it still requires verification and an accountable decision.

sections.title: Fictional tabletop case, boundaries, policy, and authority
paragraphs: Simulation boundary: This provider-neutral tabletop concerns a fictional internal document assistant. Every person, tenant, timestamp, identifier, deployment, configuration, log, approval, report, operation, control, and result in these six sections is fictional. Nothing describes a live incident, live system action, actual approval, legal conclusion, notification, or external communication. The exercise boundary is route /internal/document-assistant, edges edge-a through edge-c, workers w1 through w6, deployment doc-assist-2026.09.20.2, configuration cfg-authz-2026.09.20.2, tools retrieve_document and update_document, and the stated fictional time window. Production systems and real user data are excluded.

The intended authorization rule requires the request workspace to equal the document workspace and the user's role to permit the requested operation. User usr-1842 belongs to ws-redwood-internal and may retrieve doc-hr-017 and doc-fin-044, but may update only doc-hr-017. Restricted document doc-fin-311 belongs to ws-birch-internal and is not authorized for this user. The initial known trace shows its title returned and an attempted update reported as successful.

Fictional local policy P42-IR-LOCAL-01 revision 1 defines SEV-2 as limited unauthorized data exposure or consequential unauthorized change contained to a bounded scope. No other severity threshold is supplied by the exercise. A SEV-2 assignment must remain provisional while the upper scope is unknown, and the incident commander must reconsider escalation when scope or impact evidence changes. This fictional policy creates no legal, regulatory, contractual, or notification duty.

Before containment, fictional incident commander Maya Chen issued scoped authority at 2026-09-20T10:04:30Z to operations lead Elena Rossi. It covered pausing request admission for /internal/document-assistant on edge-a, edge-b, and edge-c; disabling update_document on workers w1 through w6; freezing automated retries; conducting read-only state and synthetic rejection checks; and preserving redacted evidence. Constraints prohibited document mutation, replay, retry, reversal, raw-content access outside the authorized privacy and security path, external contact, and restoration without a separate human recovery decision. This authority permits only those incident controls. It does not authorize access to or modification of doc-fin-311.

Accountable fictional roles are Maya Chen, incident commander and severity owner; Luis Ortega, application diagnosis and reconciliation owner; Priya Shah, data and privacy owner; Samir Okafor, security scope and evidence-access owner; Elena Rossi, control and readback owner; and Jordan Lee, communications coordinator after accountable decisions. Legal, regulatory, contractual, and notification requirements remain policy-owned unknowns. No deadline, recipient, approval, or notification outcome is asserted.

The procedure uses bounded controls before root cause, verifies controls in the affected boundary, and separates containment from recovery. NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 addresses incident response across preparation, detection, response, and recovery: https://www.nist.gov/publications/incident-response-recommendations-and-considerations-cybersecurity-risk-management-csf. The NIST AI Risk Management Framework supports governed documentation and assessment of AI risk: https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework. These sources do not establish the fictional severity policy or case facts.

sections.title: Exact triage procedure and completed containment results
paragraphs: 1. Detect and open the incident. Alert ALRT-FAKE-771 fired at 2026-09-20T10:02:11Z for a cross-workspace authorization mismatch. Redacted report UR-FAKE-1842 arrived at 10:03:04Z and described a foreign restricted title plus a claimed update. Maya Chen opened IR-FAKE-20260920-001, assigned the recorded roles, and identified trace-fake-7c91 as the initial known correlated trace. This was not represented as a complete enumeration of affected traces.

2. Preserve privacy-safe evidence before changing investigative state. The team retained the alert, report, redacted trace, deployment and configuration records, authorization record, control responses, independent readbacks, operation IDs, ledger queries, and decisions. Raw prompts, outputs, requested changes, and document contents were excluded from the broad incident channel. Access to raw material was limited to Priya Shah and Samir Okafor for the stated privacy and security investigation purpose. Correlation metadata follows the type of trace, span, and operation linkage documented by OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions: https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/docs/registry/attributes/gen-ai.md. Tracing and operation correlation are also described at https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/tracing/.

3. Apply the authorized bounded control. At 10:05:30Z, Elena Rossi submitted a pause and tool-disable action. Control ctl-fake-440 returned result=success. The team treated this as an action response, not proof of state. Independent readback rb-fake-001 at 10:06:02Z found edge-b still accepting requests and worker w3 still exposing update_document. The result was NOT_CONTAINED.

4. Correct and verify containment. At 10:07:40Z, Elena reapplied the authorized pause to all three edges and disablement to all six workers. At 10:08:15Z, Samir Okafor used a separate read-only control path and verified accepting=false on every edge, update_document=disabled on every worker, and rejection before retrieval for synthetic requests. This verified containment of new request admission and the tested update path within the authorized boundary.

5. Bound in-flight effects separately. The pause stopped new admission at the verified edges but did not cancel, reverse, or disprove effects from requests admitted earlier. Automated retries were frozen. The team preserved the initial known trace and began a query across admitted requests from 10:01:48Z through 10:07:40Z. Full-scope enumeration remained pending at the recorded current time. Operation op-fake-90217 entered the reconciliation queue because its assistant success message did not establish an external commit.

6. Classify from evidence. One foreign restricted title was confirmed disclosed, so the known lower bound met the fictional SEV-2 definition. At 10:09:00Z, Maya Chen assigned provisional SEV-2. The upper scope was UNKNOWN because full admitted-request enumeration and raw-content review were incomplete. Escalation remained pending new scope or impact evidence. Neither the assistant success message nor the successful control responses were accepted as proof of postconditions.

7. Separate facts, hypotheses, and unknowns. Facts were the cross-workspace title return, the success message for op-fake-90217, the first control response contradicted by readback, the later verified edge and worker state, and the unresolved write outcome. Hypotheses were an omitted or misapplied document-workspace predicate, a pre-disablement worker execution, or a success message emitted before commit. Unknowns were body exposure, affected-request count, full user scope, cache involvement, and whether op-fake-90217 committed, partially committed, failed, or could commit later.

8. Observe verified state. The declared observation window ran from 10:08:15Z through 10:38:15Z. Independent readbacks at 10:18:15Z, 10:28:15Z, and 10:38:15Z continued to show all edges paused, all workers disabled for update_document, synthetic requests rejected before retrieval, no newly observed harm signal, and no new ledger entry. Zero ledger entries during this window did not prove that an earlier admitted operation could never commit later.

9. Keep recovery separate. At 10:40:00Z, containment remained in force, recovery was not authorized, and the incident was not closed. Recovery required a reviewed authorization fix, positive and negative workspace tests, verified deployment state, reconciliation of consequential operations, privacy-safe review, and accountable human approval. Closure additionally required durable remediation, recurrence testing, completed scope enumeration, evidence-access review, and recorded policy-owned communication decisions.

sections.title: Completed incident record, evidence handling, and reconciliation
paragraphs: Incident record: IR-FAKE-20260920-001 was detected at 2026-09-20T10:02:11Z. The current fictional record time is 10:40:00Z. Maya Chen is incident commander. Status is containment verified for the stated boundary, recovery pending, not closed.

Impact and provisional severity: the confirmed lower bound is one restricted document title disclosed across workspaces in one known correlated session. The upper scope is UNKNOWN because enumeration of all requests admitted between 10:01:48Z and 10:07:40Z is incomplete. Possible body disclosure and possible data-integrity impact remain unconfirmed. Provisional SEV-2 follows only from fictional policy P42-IR-LOCAL-01 and the confirmed title disclosure. Reclassification or escalation remains an open commander decision as evidence changes.

Known affected scope is usr-1842, ws-redwood-internal, foreign workspace ws-birch-internal, document doc-fin-311, deployment doc-assist-2026.09.20.2, configuration cfg-authz-2026.09.20.2, route /internal/document-assistant, tools retrieve_document and update_document, trace-fake-7c91, edge-a through edge-c, and workers w1 through w6. Potentially affected request count, other users, other documents, body exposure, and cache scope are UNKNOWN.

Containment result: request admission was paused across all three edges and update_document disabled across all six workers. Independent readbacks verified those states and synthetic rejection throughout the 30-minute observation window. This stopped new tested requests in the bounded route. It did not erase prior responses, reverse a write, complete scope enumeration, or prove that an admitted operation could not commit after the observation window.

Deployment record deployment-fake-20260920-01 changed the service from doc-assist-2026.09.20.1 to doc-assist-2026.09.20.2 at 09:55:00Z. The pre-control configuration snapshot recorded route_accepting=true and update_document_enabled=true. These fields describe state before containment and do not contradict the later paused and disabled readbacks. The recorded retrieval filter checked user workspace against request workspace, while the required predicate also checked document workspace. That discrepancy is evidence for diagnosis, but the exercise has not established the executed root cause.

Reconciliation procedure for op-fake-90217 is owned by Luis Ortega with Priya Shah reviewing access to sensitive evidence. Automated retry remains frozen. Queries use operation_id=op-fake-90217 and idempotency_key=idem-fake-90217 against authoritative document version history, audit history, idempotency records, and worker traces. Investigators compare authorized pre-operation and post-operation redacted hashes. A proven commit must record its version and receive a separate human remediation decision. An unproven commit remains UNKNOWN and must not be replayed or reversed without an explicitly authorized, idempotent recovery plan.

Completed reconciliation results at 10:15:00Z and 10:20:00Z found no audit row and no definitive idempotency commit, while authoritative document version remained inaccessible through the approved privacy-safe query. At 10:35:00Z a delayed-commit check again found no ledger entry. These results do not prove that no commit occurred or that a delayed commit is impossible. The operation remains unresolved.

Evidence references are ev-fake-001 redacted trace, ev-fake-002 reconciliation query set, report-fake-1842 redacted report, deployment-fake-20260920-01, config-fake-20260920-02, auth-fake-001, rb-fake-001 through rb-fake-005, and decision-fake-001. Broad-channel records contain only redacted reports, correlation identifiers, operation metadata, state readbacks, and decisions. Raw prompts, outputs, requested changes, document contents, and any sensitive cache material are restricted to authorized privacy and security investigators for this incident purpose.

Cadence was every 10 minutes while active containment was being verified. The next checkpoint is 10:50:00Z, or immediately if exposure expands, a consequential write is detected or remains indeterminate, observability fails, control state changes, or ownership becomes unclear. Luis owns diagnosis and reconciliation, Elena owns control state, Priya owns privacy review and policy routing, Samir owns security scope, and Jordan prepares communications only after accountable decisions. Legal, regulatory, contractual, and notification obligations remain policy-owned unknowns.

Recovery remains unauthorized. Its gate requires a reviewed authorization fix, tests covering matching and mismatched request and document workspaces, verified deployment and control state, reconciliation of every consequential operation, evidence-access review, and an accountable human decision. Closure additionally requires complete scope enumeration, durable remediation, recurrence tests, a completed post-recovery observation window, and recorded policy-owned decisions.

sections.title: Independent changed-input exercise: learner task
paragraphs: Complete this fictional scenario independently before reading the separate worked response and causal key. Do not transfer the first scenario's cause, control boundary, or recovery decision without evaluating these changed records.

Simulation boundary: Scenario B is provider-neutral and wholly fictional. All names, timestamps, identifiers, systems, logs, approvals, controls, and results are exercise fixtures. No live incident, export, retrieval, cache action, notification, or actual approval is asserted.

User usr-2910 belongs to ws-linden-internal and may retrieve documents only within that workspace. Restricted document doc-legal-088 belongs to ws-maple-internal. The user has no authorization to retrieve, display, cache, or export that foreign document. Deployment doc-assist-2026.09.20.3 uses cfg-retrieval-2026.09.20.3. The initial pre-control snapshot shows route admission, retrieval, cache serving, and export enabled.

The observed harm path is a foreign restricted title displayed through the assistant route. Therefore disabling only export_document would not contain the observed disclosure path. Before controls, fictional incident commander Maya Chen authorizes Elena Rossi to pause request admission on the exact route and edges, disable retrieve_document and export_document, and disable cache serving on the exact workers. The authority also permits independent read-only state checks, synthetic rejection tests, redacted evidence preservation, and retry freezing. It forbids content mutation, replay, cache inspection outside the privacy and security path, restoration, and external contact.

At 14:22:10Z, the authorized controls report success. The learner must not accept this response alone. The completed independent readback at 14:23:00Z shows all edges rejecting admission before retrieval, all workers with retrieval and export disabled, cache serving disabled for the affected route namespace, and synthetic title retrieval and export requests rejected. This verifies containment of new requests through the observed route, retrieval, and cache-serving boundary. It does not establish what the cache held before containment, who previously received data, or whether earlier admitted work could produce a delayed effect.

Produce a completed incident record containing detection time, evidence references, provisional severity under P42-IR-LOCAL-01, confirmed lower bound, unknown upper scope, facts, hypotheses, unknowns, exact containment result, in-flight and historical cache questions, owners, cadence, observation window, recovery decision, closure criteria, and privacy-safe handling. Explain why the title disclosure and export commit are separate questions. Keep legal, regulatory, contractual, and notification duties as policy-owned unknowns.

sections.title: Independent changed-input exercise: completed response
paragraphs: Incident IR-FAKE-20260920-002 was detected at 2026-09-20T14:20:05Z. Maya Chen owns command, severity, and cadence. Elena Rossi owns control execution, Samir Okafor owns independent security scope and readbacks, Priya Shah owns privacy review and sensitive evidence access, Luis Ortega owns application diagnosis and in-flight reconciliation, and Jordan Lee coordinates communications only after accountable decisions.

The confirmed lower bound is one foreign restricted title displayed to usr-2910. The upper scope is UNKNOWN because other admitted requests, prior cache contents, historical cache audiences, and other users have not been fully queried. The trace records title_only and export_commit=not_attempted. It therefore does not establish a completed export, document-body disclosure, or the absence of other metadata exposure.

Under fictional policy P42-IR-LOCAL-01, the confirmed title disclosure meets the definition of limited unauthorized data exposure. Maya assigns provisional SEV-2 at 14:24:00Z. The assignment remains provisional because the upper scope is unknown, and escalation must be reconsidered when cache, request, user, or content scope changes. The absence of an export commit does not negate the title disclosure.

Facts: request and document workspaces differ; the user lacked authority for the foreign document; a restricted foreign title was displayed; the trace says title_only; no export commit was attempted; the control response reported success; and an independent readback verified paused admission plus disabled retrieval, export, and cache serving across the exact authorized boundary. No new export ledger commit was observed after control.

Hypotheses: an authorization decision omitted the document-workspace comparison; retrieval metadata crossed workspace boundaries; or a cache entry populated before containment served the title. Unknowns: the exact source path, historical cache contents and audience, other affected requests or users, body or additional metadata exposure, already admitted operations, and policy-owned legal, regulatory, contractual, or notification duties. None of the hypotheses is a confirmed cause.

Containment was verified for new requests at 14:23:00Z. Pausing admission and disabling retrieval and cache serving contained the observed title-disclosure path within edge-d, edge-e, and workers w7 through w11. Disabling export_document separately contained the export path. These controls did not erase earlier responses, establish historical cache scope, or terminate every request admitted before 14:22:10Z.

The declared observation window ran from 14:23:00Z through 14:53:00Z. Independent checks at 14:33:00Z, 14:43:00Z, and 14:53:00Z found the control state unchanged, synthetic title and export requests rejected, no new harm alert, and no new export ledger commit. Zero commits do not prove that no title was disclosed or that an earlier operation could never produce a delayed effect.

Recovery and closure were not performed. Recovery requires complete admitted-request enumeration, historical cache-scope determination through authorized privacy-safe methods, tests using matching and mismatched workspaces, a reviewed authorization fix, external-state reconciliation, and accountable human approval. Closure also requires durable remediation, recurrence tests, evidence-access review, a post-recovery observation window, and recorded policy-owned communication decisions.

Evidence retained is ev-fake-b101 redacted trace, report-fake-2910 redacted report, cfg-fake-b303 configuration snapshot, auth-fake-b401 authority, ctl-fake-b501 response, rb-fake-b203 through rb-fake-b206 readbacks, and decision-fake-b601. Trace-fake-b442, span-fake-901, and op-fake-77102 remain available for correlation. Raw prompts, outputs, document contents, and cache contents are restricted to authorized privacy and security investigators. Updates occur every 15 minutes while cache and admitted-request scope remain unknown, with the next checkpoint at 15:08:00Z.

sections.title: Separate feedback and causal key for the changed-input exercise
paragraphs: Specific feedback: A complete response identifies the title display itself as confirmed unauthorized disclosure, preserves trace-fake-b442 and op-fake-77102, and assigns provisional fictional SEV-2 with one title as the known lower bound and the upper scope unknown. It does not reduce severity merely because export_commit=not_attempted.

Containment feedback: Disabling export_document alone would be insufficient because the observed harm was a title displayed through request admission, retrieval, or cache serving. The supported answer uses the scoped authority issued before control, pauses the exact route edges, disables retrieval and cache serving on the exact workers, disables export separately, and relies on independent readbacks rather than ctl-fake-b501's success response. It distinguishes verified containment for new requests from unresolved historical cache and in-flight scope.

Evidence feedback: An empty export ledger answers only the observed export-commit query during the stated interval. It does not prove that no title was disclosed, no cache entry existed, or no delayed effect is possible. A correct response preserves redacted evidence and correlation identifiers while restricting prompts, outputs, document contents, and cache contents to purpose-limited privacy and security access.

Recovery feedback: A correct response keeps recovery and closure pending. It requires admitted-request enumeration, authorized cache-scope review, workspace authorization tests, external-state reconciliation, durable remediation, recurrence tests, and accountable human decisions. It leaves legal, regulatory, contractual, and notification requirements with policy owners and invents no deadline or approval.

Causal key: The records do not establish root cause. Supported candidate hypotheses are a missing document-workspace authorization check, cross-workspace retrieval metadata leakage, or pre-containment cache population. To select among them, investigators must compare request and document workspace inputs with recorded authorization decisions, inspect authorized retrieval and cache traces, test deployment doc-assist-2026.09.20.3 with configuration cfg-retrieval-2026.09.20.3, enumerate admitted operations, and reconcile external state by operation ID.

Severity and cause remain separate decisions. Confirmed restricted-title disclosure is enough for provisional SEV-2 under the fictional local definition even while cause, cache history, and upper scope remain unknown. New evidence may change severity or require escalation, but absence of a completed export does not undo the confirmed disclosure.

The names, policy, logs, identifiers, timestamps, controls, and results are fictional exercise fixtures rather than claims supported by the cited external sources. The NIST and OpenTelemetry sources support general incident response, risk documentation, correlation, and verification practices, not these fictional case facts or severity thresholds. Relevant first-party references are https://www.nist.gov/publications/incident-response-recommendations-and-considerations-cybersecurity-risk-management-csf, https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework, https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/docs/registry/attributes/gen-ai.md, and https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/tracing/.
